samples.question: The dark blocks make a landscape of columns standing on the ground, drawn as it stood before any rain. Rain water is held only where taller columns stand on both sides of it, and water that can reach either open end of the landscape runs off; one block of water fills one empty cell. Exactly one of the four columns carrying a black tag below the ground was taken away, down to the ground, before the rain fell; every other column stayed exactly as it is drawn, and the tags are numbered 1 to 4 from the left. The pale blue squares along the top count all the water the landscape holds after that column was taken away, one square for one block. Which tagged column was taken away? Answer with the tag number alone: 1, 2, 3, or 4.
